title: Platform migration deep dive
brief:
This brief exists to dominate the detail page.

We are moving three product lines off a platform that has been in place for nine years, and the piece has to be useful to two audiences at once: the operations lead who owns the timeline, and the engineer who owns the data. Start with why teams delay migrations — the cost is visible and the benefit is not — then work through the four phases we use, with the honest failure mode of each.

Phase one is inventory. Most teams underestimate it by a factor of three, because the systems nobody claims are the systems everybody depends on. Phase two is mapping, where the argument about field semantics happens; we want the piece to say plainly that this argument is the work, not a delay to the work. Phase three is the cutover rehearsal, which is where our own migration went wrong in 2024 and is worth describing in detail. Phase four is decommissioning, which nobody budgets for.

Tone: plain, specific, no vendor triumphalism. Include the eleven-day Northwind figure if it fits, but do not build the piece around it. Assume the reader has been burned before.
